correctness.rationale: Direct proof from Fourier transport: idempotency c_ψ=c_(ψ^-1)c_(ψ²) gives inversion-symmetric support, so two-dimensional right Peirce blocks have either two nonzero entries or vanish and are diagonalizable. With no order-four element, all squares lie in the odd character subgroup; cyclic squaring forces products c_ηc_(η^-1) in {0,1}, limiting eigenvalues to 0,±1. Exponent-two products are trivial and nonzero idempotents act as identity; explicit basis and uniform idempotents attain ±1 and 0 when there is an odd component. A character of order four constructs augmentation-one idempotents u_λ fixed by all right translations with a block ±λ for every λ∈C. All group sizes and zero/trivial boundaries are addressed. Independent finite exact multiplication tests on 14 examples and 188 assertions corroborate the proof but are not its basis.

value.rationale: A natural Peirce eigenvalue invariant recently resolved only for odd-order cores is now completely classified for arbitrary finite abelian cores. The order-four torsion threshold produces a striking transition from a finite set to all complex numbers with explicit idempotent witnesses. Uniform diagonalizability, exponent-two boundary and dihedral even-order consequences give a structural description relevant to nonassociative quandle-algebra decomposition, not a routine restatement of prior odd-only conclusions.
